findings.claim: The submodule bump carries a strip-layout change to ClipFramesSection (removal of the press-and-hold arrows, `flex-wrap` plus `mouse:max-h-[17.5rem] mouse:overflow-y-auto`) whose `mouse:` variant is defined nowhere, so on a mouse the strip is unbounded and the near-end sentinel is always visible, which defeats 20-at-a-time paging for both `.loft` and native panels.
findings.impact: On a desktop browser the CLIP frames panel renders every row at once (112 for an 18-minute YouTube reference, 75 for a native video) in an unbounded wrapped block rather than 20 at a time in a bounded strip. The native panel also loses its horizontal strip and arrow buttons, so it does not behave 'as before'.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/frontend/ClipFramesSection.tsx (strip className `scrollbar-hover flex flex-wrap gap-2 p-1 mouse:max-h-[17.5rem] mouse:overflow-y-auto pointer-coarse:...`). No `@custom-variant mouse` exists in frontend/src/**/*.css (grep for `variant` in frontend/src css finds only a comment at globals.css:1001), and `pointer-coarse` is the only built-in pointer variant in use. docs/process/reviews/feature-youtube-scene-tiles/decisions.md R-5 evidence: 'all 112 buttons were rendered right after the expand ... not 20 at a time; the native 75-row video ... does the same ... because the strip's `mouse:max-h-[17.5rem]` produces no CSS in the built stylesheet'. ClipFramesSection.test.tsx only regex-matches the class names (`/\bmouse:max-h-/`), so it passes whether or not the variant compiles.
findings.repro: R-5 in decisions.md: open /files/<youtube loft> on a desktop browser and expand CLIP Frames; all 112 tile buttons are in the DOM at once. Mutation: delete `mouse:max-h-[17.5rem]` from the className and the class-name test still matches the other tokens; deleting the variant from CSS cannot be caught because it was never defined.

bucket_proposal.reason: I6 requires the `.loft` panel to show '20-at-a-time paging' and the native panel to behave 'as before'. A user hits both in normal desktop use.

findings.proposed_fix: Define the `mouse` custom variant in the core stylesheet (or use an existing one such as `pointer-fine:`), or restore the bounded horizontal strip. Add a layout test against built CSS rather than a class-name regex.

specification_compliance: I1: the scene-tile route validates `t` as `float`, required, `>= 0` (422), looks the file up as the frame route does, answers 400 for a non-video, 404 for a non-`.loft` or a missing tile, and serves `tile_cache_path` with the shared `round_ms`. It writes nothing and runs no process.

I2/I3/I9: `_prepare_tiles_dir` runs after the lookup, sb0 and duration checks and removes `tiles.*`. The new directory is removed on a pre-commit failure. `_swap_tiles` runs after the commit and logs a warning naming the file id on OSError.
I4: the manifest entry is identical to the frame route's (drive_optional, file_access pre_check).
I6: violated in practice on mouse devices by the undefined `mouse:` variant (F1); the logic itself fetches on mount, guards stale responses and uses a blank block on error.
I7: SceneCandidatesSection picks scene-tile for a `.loft` filename and the frame route otherwise.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The scene-tile route answers 404 for a native video before checking the tile directory, a check the spec does not state. The observable result is the same 404.
A change of `drive` alone in the `.loft` panel refetches without resetting `timestamps`, so the previous rows stay until the new answer arrives.
The storyboard-leg tile crop skips a tile whose box falls outside a short sheet, so no row and no tile are written for it.
regression_risks: The native CLIP frames panel and the Visual Index row lose their bounded horizontal strip on desktop (undefined `mouse:` variant).
Dockerfile changes inside the submodule are not seen by the core risk classifier.
test_coverage: ClipFramesSection and VisualIndexSection layout tests only regex-match class names, so an undefined Tailwind variant passes.
test_spec_addon_079_scene_tiles.py covers the route statuses, the swap failure, leftover cleanup, the pre-commit failures and purge.
The `.loft` panel tests cover mount fetch, the stale-response guard, failed tiles and the native lazy path in jsdom only.
